extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys, agents) and pro se appellants preparing appeal briefs to the USPTO/PTAB
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory rules for preparing and filing an ex parte appeal brief to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (per MPEP §1205 / 37 CFR 41.37). Covers timing, required content, formatting, argument structure, prohibited material, and non-compliance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — Filing Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must file a brief under this section within two months from the date of filing the notice of appeal under §41.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office date of receipt of the notice of appeal (not Certificate of Mailing) measures the two-month period; Priority Mail Express deposit date counts as receipt when filed under 1.10. 37 CFR 41.37(a) does not permit filing within the time allowed for reply from the last Office action. Time may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a) (and 1.136(b) for extraordinary circumstances); ex parte reexamination uses 1.550(c). The appeal brief fee for applications and ex parte reexamination is currently set at $0 (37 CFR 41.20(b)(2)), and a brief filed on or after Jan 23, 2012 that fails to comply with 41.37(c) shall be non-compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of Failure to File Timely
rubrics_metrics.description: On failure to file the brief within the period specified (two months), the appeal will stand dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any claims stand allowed the application is not abandoned but returned to examiner for allowed claims. If no allowed claims, the application becomes abandoned as of the date the brief was due. Applicant may petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 where applicable. If appeal dismissed but application not abandoned because at least one claim is allowed, appellant may file a petition to reinstate the claims and the appeal (showing equivalent to petition to revive). Where dismissal believed erroneous, filing a petition pointing out the error may suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Content and Order (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, the brief shall contain the following items under appropriate headings and in the order indicated in paragraphs (c)(1)(i) through (v). A pro se appellant need only substantially comply with items (i), (ii), (iv), and (v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief must include items (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals, interferences, and trials; (iii) Summary of claimed subject matter; (iv) Argument; (v) Claims appendix. Headings are not required if an item is not applicable (e.g., inventor is real party in interest, or there are no related cases). A brief is compliant so long as it includes items (i)-(v) in the stated order and does not include prohibited material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real Party in Interest Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by name the real party in interest at the time the appeal brief is filed (not required if the named inventor(s) are the real party in interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If omitted, the Office may assume the named inventor(s) are real party in interest. Identification helps Board members comply with ethics/conflict rules. Example format: 'The real party in interest is XXXX corporation, the assignee of record, which is a subsidiary of a joint venture between YYYY corporation and ZZZZ corporation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Appeals, Interferences, and Trials Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by application, patent, appeal, interference, or trial number all other prior and pending appeals, interferences, trials before the Board, or judicial proceedings that (1) involve an application or patent owned by the appellant/assignee, (2) are known to appellant or counsel, and (3) may be related to or have a bearing on the Board's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are no such related cases, no statement is required; if omitted, the Office may assume there are none. The rule does not require copies of decisions in related cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Claimed Subject Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each of the rejected independent claims, with references to the specification in the Record by page and line number or paragraph number, and to the drawing by reference characters, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For claims containing means-plus-function or step-plus-function recitations under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the concise explanation must identify the structure, material, or acts described in the specification corresponding to each claimed function with precise references. Reference to the patent application publication does not satisfy this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument — Structure, Citations, and Separate Headings
rubrics_metrics.description: The arguments of appellant with respect to each ground of rejection, and the basis therefor, with citations of the statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the Record relied on; explain why the examiner erred as to each ground contested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All arguments and authorities an appellant wishes the Board to consider for the present appeal should be included in the brief (except as allowed by §§41.41, 41.47, 41.52); arguments or authorities not included will be refused consideration by the Board for purposes of the present appeal. Each ground of rejection contested must be argued under a separate heading that reasonably identifies the ground (e.g., claim number, statutory basis, applied reference). For multiple claims under the same ground, appellant may argue separately, as a group, or as a subgroup; failure to separately argue a grouped claim is a waiver of separate-patentability argument. A mere statement of what a claim recites is not an argument for patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver for Omitting Grounds or Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: If a ground of rejection stated by the examiner is not addressed in the appellant’s brief, appellant has waived any challenge to that ground and the Board may summarily sustain it (unless the examiner later withdraws the rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting that a rejection be held in abeyance (e.g., double patenting) or merely asserting a ground is improper; the brief must explain why the examiner erred. Failure to address a ground may also lead to dismissal of requests for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on New or Non-Admitted Amendments/Evidence in Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment of amendments, affidavits or other evidence filed after final action but before/on the same date of filing an appeal is governed by 37 CFR 1.116; treatment of those filed after the date of filing the appeal is governed by 41.33. Review of examiner's refusal to admit an amendment or evidence is by petition to the Director under 1.181; the time for that petition is based on the date the examiner refused entry, not the brief filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Appendix Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy of the claims should be a clean copy without markings such as brackets or underlining (except for reissue applications and reexamination proceedings), should be double-spaced, and the appendix should start on a new page. See MPEP §§1454 and rules for reexamination presentation (37 CFR 1.530(d) and (f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format, Identification, and Optional Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief should start each required item on a separate page and the brief, as well as every other document relating to an appeal, should indicate the Technology Center number and application or reexamination control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one copy of the appeal brief is required. The rule specifies minimum items but an appellant may include additional material such as list of references, table of contents, table of cases, copies of evidence entered by the examiner, etc. While not required, the Office strongly encourages an evidence appendix (copies of declarations, evidence of secondary considerations) or, at minimum, clear identification in the brief of the evidence relied upon with the date of entry into the Image File Wrapper so the Board can consider the proper evidence and avoid confusion. An example format: (A) Identification page; (B) Table of Contents; (C) Real party in interest page(s); (D) Related appeals page(s); (E) Summary of claimed subject matter; (F) Argument; (G) Claims appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Incorporation by Reference / Need for Full Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must set forth arguments and the basis therefor, with citations of statutes, regulations, authorities and parts of the Record relied upon; it is essential that the Board be provided with a brief fully stating appellant's position so no search of the Record is required to determine that position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief should not incorporate or reference previous responses; oral argument will not remedy deficiencies in a brief. Arguments presented for the first time at oral hearing are not normally entitled to consideration (except per 37 CFR 41.47).

rubrics_metrics.name: Means/Step-Plus-Function (35 U.S.C. 112(f)) Identification Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For any claim containing a means-plus-function or step-plus-function recitation as permitted by 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the concise explanation of the claimed subject matter must identify the structure, material, or acts described in the specification corresponding to each claimed function with precise references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference must be to the specification in the Record by page and line number or paragraph number, and to the drawing by reference characters; mere reference to the patent application publication does not satisfy the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arguments/Authorities Limitation to Present Appeal (and Supplemental Briefs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in §§41.41, 41.47 and 41.52, any arguments or authorities not included in the appeal brief will be refused consideration by the Board for purposes of the present appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This emphasizes that all arguments and authorities should be included in the brief; however, supplemental briefs or documents may be filed if new authority becomes available after filing (e.g., a pertinent decision published after the brief was filed). The limitation is to the present appeal and does not bar later appeals in the same application or other applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Grouping and Subgrouping Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For each ground of rejection applying to two or more claims, appellant may argue claims separately, as a group, or as a subgroup; when claims are argued as a group/subgroup, the Board may select a single claim from the group and decide the ground of rejection with respect to the group on the basis of the selected claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appellant groups claims, any claim(s) argued separately or as a subgroup must be argued under a separate subheading that identifies the claim(s) by number. Failure to separately argue claims which appellant has grouped together constitutes a waiver of any argument that the Board must consider the patentability of any grouped claim separately. To prompt separate consideration, use a subheading for each claim for which separate consideration is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Appeal Center Compliance Review and Non-Compliance Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Appeal Center (PAC) determines whether appeal briefs comply with 37 CFR 41.37 and will complete the determination before forwarding the brief to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the brief is compliant or contains only minor informalities, PAC accepts and forwards it; if non-compliant, PAC sends a notice requiring a corrected brief and appellant must file an amended brief within the time specified to avoid dismissal. If appellant disagrees with noncompliance finding, a petition under 37 CFR 41.3 may be filed (filing the petition does not toll time for reply). Once accepted by the Board as compliant, the brief will not later be held defective by PAC or the examiner. PAC will correspond directly with appellant on non-compliant issues; examiners should not use the Notification of Non-Compliant Appeal Brief (PTOL-462) or associated form paragraphs for this purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Amendments/Evidence Filed After Final or After Notice of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment or other evidence submitted under 37 CFR 1.116 or 37 CFR 41.33 will not be entered as part of the record for the appeal unless entered by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of a refusal to admit an amendment or evidence is by petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181. Petitions concerning refusals to enter amendments/evidence remain delegated according to MPEP §§1002.02(b) and (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral Argument Is Not a Substitute for a Proper Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral argument at a hearing will not remedy deficiencies in a brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments made for the first time at oral hearing are not normally entitled to consideration except as provided in 37 CFR 41.47. Ensure the brief fully states all positions and arguments with appropriate citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example Brief Format (Suggested Organizational Checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: An example brief containing the following items, each starting on a separate page: (A) Identification page; (B) Table of Contents; (C) Real party in interest page(s); (D) Related appeals, interferences, and trials page(s); (E) Summary of claimed subject matter page(s); (F) Argument page(s); (G) Claims appendix page(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1) specifies minimum requirements; appellant may include additional items (list of references, table of cases, copies of evidence entered by the examiner). The example format aids compliance and readability.
